role: Strong baselines for the Stage D sparse viscosity inverse. This file is the scoring contract. It is not a test table.
question: On the Stage A harder Burgers pilot, with the Stage D sensors32_bursts mask, does the Fourier neural operator still have lower hard_ood mean relative viscosity error than a weak-form identifier and a solver-in-the-loop fit? A negative answer is an acceptable outcome.

weak_form.name: wsin_dy_style
weak_form.citation: Messenger and Bortz, Weak SINDy for partial differential equations, arXiv:2007.02848
weak_form.description: Burgers is known. Nu is the only unknown. Each test function is separable, phi(x, t) = psi(x) eta(t), with psi and eta equal to (1 - xi^2)_+^degree. Derivatives fall on phi. The field is never differentiated. Integrals use the periodic trapezoidal rule on the sensor nodes and the trapezoidal rule in time, with half-weights on the first and last frame of each burst. Bursts are pooled into one normal equation. There is no interpolation of u.
weak_form.quadrature: periodic trapezoid in x, trapezoid in t

solver_search.returned_value: evaluated point, not an interpolated vertex
solver_search.targets: every burst except the opening burst

solver_sensor_ic.name: solver_sensor_ic
solver_sensor_ic.description: The initial condition is the real-FFT zero-pad lift of the 32 (or fewer) sensors at frame 0 onto the N=1024 grid, the same lift_sensors map as Stage D. Modes above the sensor Nyquist are zero. This is interpolation, and it is not a Burgers state. The fit then matches the true spectral solver to the sensors on the later bursts. It does not read off-sensor samples.
solver_sensor_ic.interpolation: real FFT zero-pad; coarse Nyquist coefficient halved before padding

solver_oracle_ic.name: solver_oracle_ic
solver_oracle_ic.description: The initial condition is the stored full-grid field at frame 0. The fit matches the true spectral solver to the same later-burst sensors. This ceiling reads the initial condition off the sensors. It is not a sparse-sensor estimator.

fno_reference.reason: Published per-instance estimates are reused. Checkpoints are not in git.

stress.weak_form_conditions: every condition in the Stage E protocol, all test slices
stress.notes: Weak form is scored on the full Stage E condition list at noise seed 0. The solver-in-the-loop stress is only the sensor-lift initial condition, only hard_ood, and only the four Stage E cells where the published operator mean relative error crossed 10% or the sensor count dropped. A full solver grid was outside the CPU budget. Published Stage E aggregates in the comparison columns are read from docs/v02/stage_e_scores.json by this script. They are not a new operator run. The one-burst mask has no solver target and is not in the solver list. Noise is the Stage E full-field Gaussian model. After the noisy field is built, each estimator reads only its mask.

aggregation.fno_unit: one scalar per seed per slice
aggregation.deterministic_baselines: one run; no seed standard deviation
aggregation.paired_delta: fno relative error minus baseline relative error; negative means the FNO is lower

limitations: One scalar viscosity, one-dimensional periodic Burgers, and the Stage A pilot. This is not a multi-equation benchmark.
The weak form never interpolates u. With five frames in a burst the time integral is a five-node trapezoidal rule. Degree, radius, and center stride were fixed before test scoring and were not swept.
The sensor-lift solver interpolates frame 0 only. The Stage D operator also sees frames 1 through 4. Both match the later bursts and not the opening burst.
The oracle initial-condition solver reads the full field at t = 0. It is a ceiling, not a sensor-only method.

The solver search is a 7-point coarse grid plus at most 10 golden-section steps, down to a bracket of width 0.0005. It is not an exhaustive 191-point grid. A missed local minimum would be a property of that search.
Fourier neural operator errors are the committed Stage D per-instance estimates at lambda 0. Those networks were not retrained in this run, and the published checkpoints are not in the repository.

The Fourier neural operator wall clock is one instance of the Stage D 191-point rollout with a randomly initialized network of the Stage D architecture. It measures the arithmetic, not a published checkpoint.
Solver stress covers four Stage E cells on hard_ood only. The weak form covers the full Stage E condition list at noise seed 0.
Stage E noise is scaled by the clean full-field standard deviation. The estimators then read the mask. They do not read the clean field.
not_claimed: a retuned hard_ood threshold, sensor mask, or Stage A through F protocol
a change to any previously reported number
that the weak form interpolates the sensor data onto the solver grid
that the sensor-lift initial condition is the stored field
that the oracle initial condition is available to a sensor-only method
that one Fourier neural operator seed is the result
that a negative comparison for the operator is a failure of the study
